note: Worked geolocation example: the Aundh bridge-railing roadside dump, Mapillary sequence BEohfHsAZiWFlVXwp7Gz4N, captured 17 September 2025. There is no trained detector yet, so bbox_center_x is the horizontal centre of the pile read by eye from gridded horizon strips of the 2048 x 1024 equirectangular thumbnails (pixel / 2048), accurate to roughly +/-20 px (about +/-3.5 degrees). The pile is elongated along the railing, so different frames centre on different parts of it. Positions and compass angles come from the Mapillary API (reports/visual-review/pune-aundh-adjacent-bridge/mapillary-geometry.json). The far road converges near x = 950 rather than the image centre, so heading carries about 13 degrees of uncertainty; rerun with --bearing-offset -13 to test sensitivity.
